paragraphs.text: The Inventors' Fair was a grand, month-long exposition held in the thriving city of Ghirapur , the beating heart of Avishkar 's Great Aether Boom. Billed as the pinnacle gathering for makers, dreamers, and tinkerers, the Fair drew in brilliant inventors and awestruck spectators from every corner of the plane. For the Consulate , this spectacular festival served a dual purpose: while the public marveled at ingenious new designs, the Enlightened Keepers quietly sought to collect, test, and license these technologies for broader control and distribution.

At its peak, the Inventors' Fair transformed Ghirapur into a living showcase of what artifice could achieve. From sunrise to well past sunset, the city's boulevards, plazas, and dedicated exhibition halls overflowed with dazzling displays. Gleaming constructs strode alongside crowds, airships hovered overhead, and brilliant illuminations framed the Consulate's gleaming spires.

The Inventor's Fair was a once-in-a-lifetime event organized by the Consulate to celebrate the great inventions and technological advancements made in the last century. The fairgrounds extended through all of downtown Ghirapur, filled with booths, arenas for races and other competitions, and stages for the most talented inventors to show off their creations. Along with displaying technological achievements throughout the plane, inventors compete in inventing competitions called "exhibitions".

One of the Fair's most beloved attractions was the massive artificial zoo nestled within Greenwheel . Instead of flesh-and-blood animals, the grounds teemed with lifelike constructs crafted to mimic nature's beauty. Families, children, and curious minds wandered through this interactive park, marveling at the ingenuity that blurred the line between artifice and life.
The Zoo also served as the stage for judging the Animal Constructs division of the Fair.

Speed and elegance collided on Ghirapur's racetracks. Inventors fielded all manner of vehicles, from sky skiffs to rugged ground runners. Races were the main events of many arenas, which sold out of tickets months ahead of the Fair.
The races were more than entertainment — they were a proving ground where designers tested their machines' limits and sought the attention of influential benefactors.
The Grand Exhibition the final showcase of the Inventors' Fair. The Exhibition held the final judging for inventions, and prizes were awarded to the most innovative inventors.
The Fair had over a hundred categories for inventors to enter, but there were five major categories that awarded the biggest prizes at the Fair.
Vehicles of various makes and designs were judged in the vehicle category. Vehicles will be judged on the novelty of their designs as well as their performance on the track.
Airships, skyspeeders, freighters, dragsters, barges, cruisers, and even caravans were entered in the Vehicles category.

The Fair would not have been possible without various buildings to house races and exhibitions, along with visitors from elsewhere on the plane. Not merely static displays, many of Ghirapur's newest structures were themselves submissions to the Fair's architecture division. These buildings combined a practical purpose with stunning visual splendor. Graceful arches, dynamic lighting arrays, and moving parts reflected the city's devotion to marrying aesthetics with function, making places like Artani Hall attractions in their own right.
Submissions for the Architecture category included arenas, demonstration stages, and hotels.

Perhaps the category of most interest to the Consulate, the domain of aether science pushed the boundaries of what was possible. This category invited theorists and engineers alike to imagine new ways to refine, channel, and manipulate the volatile energy. Staged demonstrations allowed participants to show off their work before judges and the public.
Innovations in refinement methods, power extraction, and even teleportation were presented, each vying for recognition from the Consulate's Enlightened Keepers.
Under careful watch, inventors demonstrated new weaponry for both civilian and security applications. Each weapon's performance was rated and judged by Consulate professionals.

From discreet personal defense tools to towering aether cannons, each device was tested and judged for its originality, safety, and potential value to the Consulate's interests. The Weapons category included multiple subcategories, including Long-Range, Personal Defense, Aether-Firing, Vehicle-Attachment, and Construct-Attachment.
While not the most practical, the Animal Constructs category proved among the most popular.
Constructs competed in feats of agility, speed, and strength to win top prizes.

The true stars were the inventors themselves. They came from all walks of life — humble backyard tinkerers, visionary crafters, and Consulate-approved designers alike. With an abundant supply of aether, they brought to life wild ideas that might otherwise have remained dreams.

While the inventors competed for prizes, benefactors competed for the inventors. Investors and patrons wandered the exhibits, ready to stake fortunes on the next transformative breakthrough. For some, the right deal struck at the Fair could shape Kaladesh's future.

Every creation needed the approval of the Fair's panel of judges — wise, exacting, and instantly recognizable by their faces painted red. Their decisions elevated unknown innovators to citywide fame or dashed hopes in an instant. To win a judge's favor was to gain prestige that could last a lifetime.

The Fair belonged to the people as much as to the inventors. Citizens from every district, along with travelers from distant parts of Kaladesh, crowded Ghirapur's avenues to glimpse the wonders on display. For them, the Fair was a month-long spectacle of marvels and dreams made real.
The Consulate scheduled the Inventors' Fair and began preparations six months ahead of the Fair's start.

When the construction of the Inventors' Fairgrounds started, the allocation of aether to "under-utilized neighborhoods" was reduced by Consulate decree. This was meant to be temporary, an emergency precautionary measure to ensure the Fair's safety. However, the reduction in aether upset the citizens and inventors of Kaladesh, inciting revolutionary support.
paragraphs.section: Construction of the Fairgrounds and aether distribution

paragraphs.text: In the weeks leading up to the Fair, preparations for the Fair became repeatedly disrupted by renegades. Despite the Consulate's best efforts, its enforcers were unable to discover and eliminate the renegade force. As a result, Senior Consulate Inspector and planeswalker Dovin Baan traveled to Ravnica the day before the Fair began to ask for the Gatewatch 's aid in rooting out the renegade cause. The Gatewatch clarified that their organization was focused on issues of planewalkers and threats from without, and couldn't assist with an issue that was internal to a specific plane. However, one member of The Gatewatch, Chandra Nalaar , was born on Kaladesh and remembered the tyrannical practices of the Consulate and its role in her parents' deaths. She planeswalks to Kaladesh, quickly followed by Lilliana Vess . Later, after Dovin hears Chandra's last name, he reveals her past on Kaladesh, before Lavinia reports to the rest of the Gatewatch that Chandra and Liliana planeswalked away.

After finding out about Chandra's departure, Dovin and Nissa travel to Kaladesh, where Dovin gets Consulate reinforcements, and they track down Chandra to find Head Judge Tezzeret confronting Renegade Prime - Pia Nalaar - along with Liliana and Chandra. Despite Chandra, Liliana, and Nissa opposing the Consulate reinforcements, Pia was forced to surrender to Consulate custody.
At the height of the Grand Exhibition, Pia was paraded in front of a jeering and heckling crowd.
paragraphs.section: Quicksmithing duel between Tezzeret and Renegade Prime

paragraphs.text: Tezzeret enacted his final act as head judge, initiating the artificer's duel with Pia Nalaar. Although Pia was a supremely skilled artificer and held her own, Tezzeret was a master of metal and had magical abilities Pia could never hope to match. Then suddenly, Tezzeret sent an attack at Pia that was clearly intended to kill her.
paragraphs.section: Quicksmithing duel between Tezzeret and Renegade Prime

paragraphs.text: She was saved only by the sudden intervention from Chandra, who abandoned her disguise and charged at Tezzeret, sending fireballs to melt his metal constructs as the crowd started panicking in the stands. Consulate guards streamed onto the arena floor to defend the head judge, heavily outmanning Chandra, but Chandra had companions of her own. The Gatewatch all joined the fighting, quickly coming to Pia's aid while putting pressure on Tezzeret and his guards.
paragraphs.section: Quicksmithing duel between Tezzeret and Renegade Prime

paragraphs.text: While the crowd was distracted by all of these events, a quieter event was happening to the side, where Consulate enforcers, acting on Tezzeret's orders, seized all the wondrous prizes submitted for judging in the Inventors' Fair. As the crowds fled the arena, the inventors were shocked to realize their works had all been seized by the Consulate "for safekeeping". The Consulate's official position was that, as a whole, the inventions posed a threat to the citizens of Ghirapur, since they were all unproven and had not been submitted through the Consulate's rigorous battery of tests. The artifacts were taken away, and Tezzeret withdrew to a secretive laboratory in the Aether Spire with Rashmi's space-folding device, which would allow the transport of non-organic material through planar space. Tezzeret planned to develop this technology to be able to pass through extraplanar space, creating a Planar Bridge .
